doc.subject: Mironet swaps Claude for Jev; Macaly ships BYO-agent infra
doc.verdict: Mironet’s Jev swap shows where LLM agents lose. Macaly is turning Claude and ChatGPT into a deployment surface. Security buyers now ask about agent permissions, not demos.

items.headline: Mironet replaced Claude agents with Jev, cutting categorization costs 343×.
paragraphs: In the “cost per workflow” shift, Mironet moved product categorization off LLM agents and onto Jev, a typed decision model that returns structured verdicts instead of prose.

The interesting part is the architecture move: treat the generative model as the messy-edge worker, then put fast, calibrated gates in front of every expensive step. Jev’s early adoption on Vercel suggests this pattern will spread beyond e‑commerce.

block.head: Mironet’s split: LLM agents for text, Jev for decisions
block.lead: A concrete before/after showing how “typed decisions” replace LLM agents in a structured workflow.

items.means: Typed decision models can become the default “control plane” around an LLM, shrinking both verification labor and model spend in any structured workflow.

items.headline: Macaly Cloud made Claude/ChatGPT deployments one-click, free until 1 October.
paragraphs: In the “bring your own agent” fight, Macaly Cloud is trying to win by owning setup and deployment while letting users stay inside Claude or ChatGPT. Its latest update removes manual database, hosting, auth, and emailing setup and exposes the stack through an MCP connector.

Macaly is also setting an explicit price anchor for the infra layer, with $10/month after the trial. Together with its earlier “publish from chat” launch and team.blue distribution, the bet is that project state and deployment become the moat, not the chat UI.

points.text: Macaly Cloud is introduced as a way to publish apps/sites from Claude or ChatGPT.
Macaly sharpens the “shared infrastructure” framing and “avoid paying twice.”
Coverage adds scale context and a concrete “prompt-to-live app” demo claim.
A new update removes manual setup steps and offers a free trial until 1 October.

block.head: How Macaly moved from “publish from chat” to “own setup”
block.lead: A short sequence of public statements that set up the “open infrastructure” positioning.

items.means: If your customers build in Claude/ChatGPT, you either become a callable capability inside that workspace or you become the deployment layer that makes “done” real.

items.headline: Cequence said billing agents get 105 tools when they need four.
paragraphs: Cequence framed agent governance as continuous control, not occasional checks, and claimed billing assistants are commonly given 105 tools when only four are needed. In a separate warning, it said enterprise AI accounts have grown 100X and many lack an owner or expiration.

items.headline: Petra Stupková warned Czech leaders to treat AI pace as risk.
paragraphs: Petra Stupková argued that AI development has accelerated unexpectedly fast and pointed to recent incidents as warning signs. She framed “responsibility” as a condition for sustainable adoption, not an anti-innovation stance.
